messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU serving queue length > 10k across prod-cluster-us-west-2. Tokenized latency alarm tripped. Paging on-call. (alert_id: gpu_queue_critical)
Maya (on-call SRE): Acknowledged. I'm on it — looking at autoscaler logs and nodegroups now.
Jun (infra): I got the page too, jumping in. Early look: cluster-autoscaler is trying to create nodegroup 'gpu-pool-2' but failing with launch template/IAM errors in ASG events.
Maya (on-call SRE): Can you paste the error? I see pods pending with reason: "Insufficient GPUs" and queue backlog growing.
Jun (infra): Paste of `kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/cluster-autoscaler`:
```
I0521 22:24:10.123456 1 scale.go:123] Failed to autoscale: error creating launch configuration: UnauthorizedOperation: You are not authorized to perform this operation
	status code: 403, request id: abc-123
```
Jun (infra): Looks like the instance-profile for autoscaler/cloudformation role lost the EC2:RunInstances permission when a recent launch-template change rolled out.
Priya (runtime): Traffic note: we saw a 3x spike in long-context generation jobs from a single tenant around 22:20 which saturated GPU queues. We had lower-priority batch jobs enqueued alongside latency-sensitive requests.
Maya (on-call SRE): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) throttle/evict noncritical batch pods, 2) scale up a separate preemptible GPU nodegroup we can create manually, 3) if autoscaler fix ETA > 10m we manually create nodes and drain/pod-schedule. Jun, can you confirm manual node creation steps?
Jun (infra): On it. I'll create a temporary nodegroup 'gpu-emergency-ephemeral' using an older launch-template version that has working IAM. Creating now via `aws eks create-nodegroup` with `--launch-template Name=lt-prod-gpu,Version=3` and attaching proper node-role.
Jun (infra): Also noting taint/labels: prod GPU pools have `node.kubernetes.io/gpu: true:NoSchedule` plus `redwood:gpu=dedicated`. Some pods are tolerant-less. For quick relief I can apply a toleration to the priority controller to land latency-critical pods.
Priya (runtime): Please don't remove the taint globally — that would let low-priority jobs take GPUs. Use a toleration patch for the runtime podspecs we mark critical. I can push a quick rollout to add tolerations to the `realtime-serving` deployment.
Alex (oncall): I'll coordinate support comms. Nora, can you draft a customer-facing note? We have 3 active customers seeing increased 500s for streaming responses.
Nora (support): Drafting: "We are actively mitigating an infrastructure issue causing increased latency and errors for GPU-backed endpoints in us-west-2. We expect partial recovery within 20–30 minutes; we'll update in 10 minutes." Will post to status.redwood.ai once we have recovery.
Maya (on-call SRE): Live commands I'm running (sensitive bits redacted):
```
# cordon non-critical nodes to free up schedulers
kubectl label nodes --selector=role=batch batch-drain=now
kubectl scale deploy realtime-serving -n prod --replicas=0   # temporary to free GPUs for migration
```
Maya (on-call SRE): Also increasing queue timeouts and applying rate-limit throttle at the edge so new long jobs are rejected with 429 rather than piling up.
Jun (infra): `create-nodegroup` returned in 80s; new nodes joining ASG now. kubelet registrations starting: `10.0.2.45`, `10.0.2.46` with GPU resources.
deploy-bot: New nodes registered: gpu-emergency-ephemeral-1, gpu-emergency-ephemeral-2 :white_check_mark:
Priya (runtime): Realtime-serving toleration rollout applied. K8s scheduled a few critical pods onto new nodes. Confirming lower queue depth on the GPU scheduler.
Maya (on-call SRE): Observability: queue length dropped from 10.2k -> 1.8k over 4 minutes. Latency percentiles improving. Good sign.
Jun (infra): Root cause: a recent infra change (launch-template v4) removed a required IAM policy addition to the node/instance role; cluster-autoscaler didn't have permissions to create new launch-config/lt version. Rolling back LT to v3 and pushing a fix to role perms.
Maya (on-call SRE): Next: Jun will push IAM fix + verify cluster-autoscaler create events. Priya will keep monitoring scheduling and ensure no eviction storms. I'm going to handoff after 30 minutes to Alex for secondary monitoring.
Alex (oncall): Taking handoff at 22:58 UTC — will monitor for 60m and let PG know when fully healed.
Nora (support): Posted status on status.redwood.ai: "Partial service degradation for GPU-backed endpoints in us-west-2. Mitigation in progress; updates in 15 mins." Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/RED-2026-0421
Maya (on-call SRE): Post-incident actions captured: 1) revert LT v4 and add automated IAM unit test for launch-template role, 2) add autoscaler permission healthcheck, 3) add quota alerting for GPU pool and separate throttles for batch vs realtime, 4) document manual nodegroup creation playbook in eng-infra runbooks.
Priya (runtime): We'll also add runtime-level backpressure to prevent large tenant batch floods from saturating GPU queues.
Jun (infra): Change merged to restore IAM perms. Cluster-autoscaler now creates node groups successfully in dry-run. I'll follow up with an infra PR for LT validation.
Maya (on-call SRE): Marking as recovering. Will keep thread open until metrics stable for 30m. If anything regresses ping me directly. :thumbsup:
Alex (oncall): Monitoring OK at T+45m. Queue stable <500 and tail latency within SLOs. Handing back to Maya for postmortem writeup tomorrow.
incident-bot: Incident status updated: RECOVERING -> MONITORED. Incident assigned: eng-infra, eng-sre. Priority: P1 (reduced).
